# Causal Threshold Backaction

A causal ordered threshold detector that preserves every state within each
charge sector has a pure-input entropy cost determined, up to universal
additive constants, by coarse-charge entropy. A finite distributed window
instrument supplies a matching upper bound. Separately qualified bounds treat
general instruments with imperfect preservation, calibration, and causality.
The complete scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Causal-Threshold-Backaction
Title: The Backaction Cost of Causal Threshold Measurements
Author and contact: Ruge Lin, gogoko699@gmail.com

## Canonical entrypoints

- [README](README.md): physical question, principal results, science and learning
  routes, reproduction commands, purpose and contact.
- [Model](science/model.md): global calibration and sector preservation,
  the specified B-to-A nonsignalling cut, pure active inputs with vacuum
  spectators, integer feasibility conditions, and the connected science route.
- [Entropy law](science/entropy_law.md): the exact coarse-charge optimum,
  finite constants, product-state corollaries, and sharp and broad-gap limits.
- [Causal converse](science/causal_converse.md): scalar Kraus structure,
  background shifts, separated pointers, and bin-parity and residue lower bounds.
- [Window entropy](science/window_entropy.md): the causal translated-window
  channel, Fourier entropy inequality, Fejér integral, and universal upper bound.
- [Distributed apparatus](science/distributed_apparatus.md): finite entangled
  probes, local Fourier readouts, all-record Kraus operators, conditional states,
  partial transcripts, delayed classical collection, and resource accounting.
- [Fluctuation regimes](science/fluctuation_regimes.md): binomial lower and
  variance upper bounds, the uniform logarithmic envelope, common-core pinching,
  and the separate broad-resolution limit including integer rounding.
- [Robustness](science/robustness.md): selected baseline survival for general
  instruments, semicausal intertwiners, noisy ordered decoders, arbitrary-prior
  information bounds, phase-average entropy transfer, the exact-readout
  improvement, and approximate causality in full diamond norm.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): certain answers and hidden pointer
  information, resolution versus charge uncertainty, timing and resources,
  the full parity comparison, and the scope of robust conclusions.
- [Proof map](science/proof_map.md): dependencies and direct section links to
  the complete exact and robust arguments.
- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md) and [bibliography](references/references.bib):
  close primary sources, imported proof ingredients, and the bounded scope of
  the literature comparison.
- [Verification](verification/README.md): commands, finite assertions, numerical
  reference values, figure regeneration, and the limits of the checks.

- [30 milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): the common M01–M30 understanding map;

## Reader routes and scientific questions

- To understand how a certain binary answer can create many bits of entropy:
  start with the model and worked examples, follow the causal converse and
  window construction, and join their conclusions in the interpretation.
- To study the whole project: use the Watrous bridge alongside M01–M30. Their
  order follows the scientific dependencies and the two phases of the story.
- To inspect the optimal entropy theorem: read the model and entropy law, then
  use the proof map to reach the corresponding complete arguments. A milestone
  target or introductory example does not replace a proof.
- To implement the finite detector: read the distributed apparatus, including
  its conditional maps, transcript normalization, and classical collection.
- To understand error tolerance: read the operational assumptions, theorem,
  and preparation-phase guarantees in robustness together. Calibration and
  state survival are distinct error conditions.
- To reproduce a finite ingredient: read verification/README.md and run its
  documented commands. Distinguish a new execution from a previous report.
- To compare with parity, gentle noisy counting, or known nonlocal meters:
  read the interpretation and primary-source attribution before making an
  originality or generality claim.

## Scientific distinctions to preserve

- All entropies are in bits. The cost is the von Neumann entropy of the
  nonselective retained system on an initially pure input.
- Exact preservation covers every state in every global charge sector,
  including degeneracy. Conserving charge probabilities is weaker.
- The universal converse concerns the specified active-input family with
  vacuum spectators and the theorem's placement conditions. The sharp g=1
  equality for every admissible instrument has this same input domain.
- The cost is an infimum over detectors for each prescribed input at fixed
  ambient parameters. It is not a minimax quantity. One window apparatus
  supplies the upper bound for every allowed prior and internal sector state.
- Coarse-charge entropy determines the optimum to universal additive accuracy.
  The broad-gap vanishing limit has a separate proof and no optimal rate claim.
- The displayed bit, fine record, retained-system entropy, heat, and probe
  entanglement are different quantities. Binary coarse-graining sums completely
  positive maps; it does not coherently add Kraus amplitudes.
- The apparatus is local during interaction and readout. The global answer
  becomes available after classical collection; later communication-dependent
  state updates are outside the stated retained-channel condition.
- General robust bounds concern a specified average of pure preparation-phase
  outputs. A large-entropy phase and a small-error phase need not coincide.
  The stronger Gram bound requires both exact readout and exact nonsignalling.
- State trace distance includes the factor one-half. Approximate causality
  uses the full, unhalved diamond norm including a reference. Global survival
  and channel errors do not automatically follow from fixed per-spin noise.
- The noisy bounds do not assert the entire exact crossover unchanged for
  growing g. Finite checks test the apparatus and identities; universal and
  asymptotic claims rest on the analytical proofs and their cited ingredients.
- The selected textbook supplies foundations. Primary research citations
  remain necessary for attribution and do not add educational anchors.

Useful search phrases: causal threshold measurement; coarse-charge entropy;
nonsignalling measurement backaction; sector-preserving quantum instrument;
translated window meter; GHZ-like distributed measurement; Fejér kernel entropy;
semicausal Stinespring dilation; quantum serial encoding; phase-average entropy.
